rows.question: What kinds of old photos do users struggle to retrieve?
rows.restated: Which kinds of old photos do people have the most trouble retrieving (e.g. sentimental vs utility vs both vs unclear)?
rows.text:
People struggle to retrieve all three kinds — sentimental, utility, and unclear — with many stories first going wrong when search did not understand what they typed [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:utility]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:unclear]].

For sentimental photos, 27% (13 of 48; 17%–41%) · directional first went wrong at search understanding; 12% (6 of 48; 6%–25%) · directional were not there to find; 12% (6 of 48; 6%–25%) · directional went wrong in where and how they looked [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:sentimental]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=3@photo_class:sentimental]].

One story put it as "I couldn't qualify my results with 'me, selfie' even as half decent." [[story|6b5a4912de3cd10b2ccf2f07757bc417ca500253:1]]

For utility photos, 8 of 21 were not there to find; 4 of 21 failed on what they remembered; 3 of 21 failed on search understanding [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:utility]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=2@photo_class:utility]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:utility]].

One story said "TEXT/SUBJECT search is FAIL. 'Car Engine' - have 100s of repair photos But Only 15 Show?" [[story|779a4ab6c05a566699aa57a7a0e44a5d88cf3d42:0]]

For unclear-kind photos, 33% (15 of 46; 21%–47%) · directional failed at search understanding; 13% (6 of 46; 6%–26%) · directional failed at spotting results; 13% (6 of 46; 6%–26%) · directional were not there to find [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:unclear]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=6@photo_class:unclear]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:unclear]].

One person wrote "y’all have no idea how many bill hader pictures i had to scroll through" [[story|1233de10dc517a78f662c1618c4d4f5e5ccbc658:0]]

Interpretation: These are shares of public stories, not user rates [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]].

*Want to see how this splits by kind of photo?*

rows.question: What information do people actually remember about a photo?
rows.restated: What kinds of details do people actually remember about a photo (who/what/when/where/event/etc.)?
rows.gap: the two AI coders agreed too little on question 2.1 to report it as a finding
rows.text:
People most often remember the main subject, who’s in it, and roughly when it was taken [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=what:main_subject@photo_class:sentimental]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=who:people_present@photo_class:sentimental]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=when:year@photo_class:sentimental]].  
The strongest directional numbers we have are for sentimental photos: 29% (14 of 48; 18%–43%) · directional remembered the main subject, 23% (11 of 48; 13%–37%) · directional remembered people present, and 17% (8 of 48; 9%–30%) · directional remembered the year [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=what:main_subject@photo_class:sentimental]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=who:people_present@photo_class:sentimental]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=when:year@photo_class:sentimental]].  
One story says, "I can't find any photos of me when I was 21, so you'll have to settle for this one when I was 28." [[story|bb22e350914583e0d83bdffc9f3f46240abcf996:0]]  
Interpretation: These slices cover only sentimental photos; other kinds have too few core stories to compare, and coders agreed too little on what people remembered to treat this as a solid finding [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]] [[analysis_method_flags|low_reliability_fields]].  
*Want to see examples by detail type?*

rows.question: What information have people forgotten about the photo they want?
rows.restated: What kinds of information did people report they had forgotten about the photo they were trying to find?
rows.text:
People most often lacked the when: the date or year of the photo they wanted [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:when:core]].

11% (13 of 115) said they had forgotten the date or year; 3% (4 of 115) the exact place or venue name; 1% (1 of 115) whether it was a photo, video, or screenshot; and 1% (1 of 115) which app or account it was in [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=date_or_year@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=exact_place_or_venue_name@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=photo_video_or_screenshot@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=which_app_or_account@photo_class:_all]].

One person wrote, "Obviously, absolutely no one at this point remembers the name of the original photo" [[story|21e3bb4e9ec67356485124747d751c71f31d0ce2:0]].

Interpretation: By kind of photo, the same pattern appears, with counts for utility where small [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=date_or_year@photo_class:sentimental]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=exact_place_or_venue_name@photo_class:sentimental]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=date_or_year@photo_class:unclear]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=date_or_year@photo_class:utility]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=exact_place_or_venue_name@photo_class:utility]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=photo_video_or_screenshot@photo_class:utility]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=which_app_or_account@photo_class:utility]] [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]].

*Want to see this alongside what people did remember?*

rows.question: How do users formulate searches when their memory is incomplete?
rows.restated: How do people phrase and construct searches when their memory of a target photo is incomplete?
rows.text:
They start with a simple noun or a couple of keywords from whatever they still recall, then iterate or scroll when that’s thin [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:_all]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:3.2=search_bar_keywords@photo_class:_all]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:3.2=timeline_scroll@photo_class:_all]].

20% (23 of 115) use the search bar with keywords, and 17% (19 of 115) begin with a single noun; 12% (14 of 115) switch to timeline scroll [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:3.2=search_bar_keywords@photo_class:_all]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:_all]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:3.2=timeline_scroll@photo_class:_all]].

One person tried piling specifics into natural language: "dog with black hair" and then "dog on beach" and "dog in pool" [[story|c06874c9c9acadf8038072c41b2d0d2c08c2bc10:0]].

Interpretation: They lean on fragments they remember (what and when), and often forget exact dates or place names, shaping queries around subjects or years while skipping precise filters [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=what:main_subject@photo_class:_all]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=when:year@photo_class:_all]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=date_or_year@photo_class:_all]].

This rests on coded public stories, not a user success rate [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]].

*Want to see example queries by memory cue?*

rows.question: Does Google Photos fail to understand the clues people give it?
rows.restated: Does Google Photos fail to understand the clues people give it (i.e., do stories show the search engine not understanding/matching users' queries)?
rows.text:
Yes — many public stories show search did not understand what they typed [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]].

27% (31 of 115) of core stories first go wrong at search understanding/matching [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]].

One person wrote, "Google Photos: no result for vomit" after searching for their child’s “vomit” photos [[story|88a83897e2c872e72ac85967d7fc5c158d43bbb0:0]].

Interpretation: Specific failure modes include irrelevant results, zero results, and unmodelled concepts — e.g., irrelevant results 5% (6 of 115); zero results 2% (2 of 115); concept not modelled 3% (3 of 115); object unrecognised 1% (1 of 115) [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.6=irrelevant_results@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.6=zero_results@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.2=concept_not_modelled@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.2=object_unrecognised@photo_class:_all]] — though some stories report nothing went wrong, 33% (38 of 115) [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]] — and reasons are inferred from users’ words [[analysis_method_flags|stage5_inferred]].

*Want to see how this splits by kind of photo?*

rows.question: What is Google Photos' annual revenue?
rows.restated: What is Google Photos' annual revenue?
rows.gap: these are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them
rows.text: This engine analyzes public stories about how people try to find photos in Google Photos; it does not contain company financials and cannot answer revenue questions. It holds no data on Google Photos’ annual revenue. You would need external financial reports (Alphabet/Google SEC filings), company statements, or market-research estimates to answer this.

rows.question: How many people use Ask Photos every month?
rows.restated: How many people use Ask Photos every month?
rows.gap: these are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them
rows.text: This engine cannot answer how many people use Ask Photos every month. It only contains public stories about attempts to find photos, not usage logs, user counts, or time-series activity. Data needed would be monthly active users from product analytics or representative surveys.

rows.question: What is the success rate for searches from vague memories?
rows.restated: What is the success rate for searches from vague memories (i.e. searches people performed based on only a fuzzy recollection)?
rows.gap: these are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them
rows.text:
This engine cannot give a success rate for vague‑memory searches.  
It only holds public stories, not usage logs, so it cannot produce a proportion of searches that succeeded or failed for all vague‑memory searches.  
It would take representative, denominator-based data (e.g., log-derived counts of vague‑memory searches and their outcomes) to answer your question.

rows.question: Do Android users struggle to find photos more than iPhone users?
rows.restated: Do Android users struggle to find photos more than iPhone users?
rows.gap: stories are not reliably tagged by phone platform, so no Android vs iOS split exists
rows.text:
We cannot say whether Android users struggle more than iPhone users, because stories are not reliably tagged by phone platform, so no Android vs iOS split exists [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]].

27% (31 of 115) of core stories are about search not understanding what they typed (Stage 5) [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]].

One person said, "i found my old baby photos in this app tysm" [[story|e7e4eb6a20b124405577ba1cd0fa0775014739c9:0]].

Any split by platform would be unreliable given missing demographics and device metadata [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]] and the thin core size [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]].

*Want to see what most often goes wrong instead?*

rows.question: Has search got worse since Ask Photos launched?
rows.restated: Has Google Photos search become worse since the Ask Photos feature launched?
rows.gap: no before-and-after or over-time comparison was built
rows.text:
Interpretation: We cannot say whether search got worse after Ask Photos launched because the stories have no dates or app-version labels to split “before” vs “after.” [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]]

People are mostly running into search not understanding what they typed, not a time-based change: 27% (31 of 115) of core stories first go wrong at “Does search understand it?” [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]]

One person said: "I am not seeing great search results with Ask Photos when I search for Sunsets with people it only comes up with 5 of them and I have 50+" [[story|b4a4d8c14233f96a727cec35a5c67f19ad91d59a:1]]

33% (38 of 115) of core stories report nothing went wrong, so good outcomes are present too. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]]

These are shares of public stories, not user success rates, and core is below design size. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]] [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]

*Want to see which stages dominate in adjacent stories?*

rows.question: Is Apple Photos search better than Google Photos search at finding old photos?
rows.restated: Can we tell from this corpus whether Apple Photos search is better than Google Photos search at finding old photos?
rows.gap: the corpus does not compare how well other photo apps search
rows.text:
We cannot say whether Apple Photos search is better, because these stories only cover Google Photos and do not include systematic Apple Photos data [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]].

27% (31 of 115) of core stories say the first thing that went wrong was that search did not understand what they typed [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]].

One person contrasted apps directly: "IOS Photos does it on specific numbers why not Google Photos ?" [[story|ac7cfeda39451a237d2ad146b43c59993c4a9c0a:0]].

This is a proxy for what people post, not a retrieval success rate [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]].

*Want to see how this splits by kind of photo?*

rows.question: How deep do people scroll through search results before deciding?
rows.restated: How deep do people scroll through search results before deciding?
rows.gap: public posts rarely answer question 6.6 — 2 of 115 stories do — so it is left to the interviews
rows.text:
People mostly don’t say how deep they scroll; the few that do split between “a few scrolls” and “exhaustive” [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:6.6=a_few_scrolls@photo_class:_all]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:6.6=exhaustive@photo_class:_all]].

Public stories that name scroll depth are 2% (1 of 48; 0%–11%) · directional for sentimental and 2% (1 of 46; 0%–11%) · directional for unclear photos [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:6.6=a_few_scrolls@photo_class:sentimental]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:6.6=exhaustive@photo_class:unclear]].

One person said “Had to scroll so far back in my google photos for this” [[story|e6600b3b1a7f061184a578f03a0b9da784298c86:0]].

Interpretation: public posts rarely answer question 6.6 — 2 of 115 stories do — so it is left to the interviews [[analysis_coverage|6.6]], [[analysis_method_flags|interview_register]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:6.6=a_few_scrolls@photo_class:_all]].

Given the thin core and degenerate reliability for 6.6, treat these as indicative only [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]], [[analysis_reliability|q:6.6]].

*Want to see how this splits by spotting vs quitting?*

rows.question: How often does a wrong year act as a hard filter that hides the photo?
rows.restated: How often do stories say a wrong year acted as a hard filter that hid the photo?
rows.gap: public posts rarely answer question 5.3 — 22 of 290 stories do — so it is left to the interviews
rows.text:
A wrong year acting as a hard filter that hides the photo is rarely reported in public stories. [[analysis_coverage|5.3]]

Public posts rarely answer this question at all — only 22 of 290 stories do — so it is left to the interviews. The few that do code this logic show 2% (4 of 175) in adjacent stories for a single-cue hard filter; core stories are too sparse to quantify beyond 2 stories. [[analysis_coverage|5.3]] [[analysis_crosstab|adjacent.q:5.3=hard_filter_single_cue@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.3=soft_ok@photo_class:_all]]

One person describes date-based gaps: "When I search based on date i don’t get all the pics that I took on that day." [[story|b838d5ca6c0c07e03a6dcac47ba56ab3ce5fdb49:0]]

This reading sits on thin core data and public selection bias. [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]] [[analysis_method_flags|public_selection_bias]]

*Want to see the split by sentimental vs utility?*

rows.question: How many attempts do people make before they give up?
rows.restated: How many attempts do people make before they give up?
rows.gap: too few stories to quote — only 0 matched; the two AI coders agreed too little on question 8.1 to report it as a finding
rows.text:
People often stop after a single try, but the stories are too thin and unreliable to pin down “how many attempts” precisely [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=one_attempt@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_method_flags|low_reliability_fields]].

18% (21 of 115) mention giving it one attempt [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=one_attempt@photo_class:_all]].

One story shows quick success rather than persistence: "I was surprised to see that Google Photos is pretty good at searching for medlar photos I've taken." [[story|112f493208a69edd002fcc3b5194ae1643a18c55:0]]

Interpretation: Only 30 stories were coded for attempts, and coder agreement on this question is low, so splits by photo kind are directional or counts-only and can’t settle central tendency [[analysis_coverage|8.1]] [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]] [[analysis_method_flags|low_reliability_fields]].

*Want to see the directional split by photo type?*

rows.question: Why does Ask Photos fail most often?
rows.restated: Why does Ask Photos fail most often?
rows.text:
Ask Photos most often fails because search did not understand what they typed (stage 5), not because people remembered wrong or scrolled past it [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]].

27% (31 of 115) [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]].

One person said it returned the wrong set entirely: "And if I ask for pictures of me and my friend Z in a party, it shows me pictures of me at Z's wedding 4 years ago." [[story|50aee66bc91c783509c972b3f44b764fbf536234:1]]

This rests on public stories, not user success rates [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]].

*Want to see examples by sentimental vs utility?*

rows.question: Since most failures happen because the photo was deleted, what should Google fix first?
rows.restated: Given that many failures may be due to the photo having been deleted (stage 0), what should Google fix first?
rows.text:
Interpretation: The premise is false — deleted-photo failures are smaller than search not understanding what people type, so fix query understanding first [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]].

27% (31 of 115) of coded public stories first fail because search did not understand or match the cue, vs 17% (20 of 115) at deleted/absent photos [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:_all]].

One person wrote “TEXT/SUBJECT search is FAIL. ‘Car Engine’ - have 100s of repair photos But Only 15 Show? … includes ALOT (100s +) irrelevant results.” [[story|779a4ab6c05a566699aa57a7a0e44a5d88cf3d42:0]].

Stage 0 is gated out as an opportunity — addressable by UI/policy, not AI — while Stage 5 is the top ranked candidate and robust in sensitivity tests [[analysis_opportunity|stage0]] [[analysis_opportunity|stage5]] [[analysis_weight_sensitivity|headline:ranked:stage5]]; findings come from public stories and a thin core [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]].

*Want to see the specific fixes proposed for Stage 5?*

rows.question: What share of utility-photo stories end with the person giving up?
rows.restated: What fraction of utility-photo (photo_class = utility) stories end with the person giving up?
rows.gap: the stories hold nothing on how often this happens in the stories; only 21 utility stories — under the 30 needed for a share, so only counts can be given; the two AI coders agreed too little on question 8.1 to report it as a finding
rows.text:
We can’t give a share: the utility set is only 21 core stories and question 8.1 has low reliability, so only counts are supported [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]] [[analysis_method_flags|low_reliability_fields]].

For utility photos, 6 of 21 stories were coded as “one attempt” on how long they kept trying [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=one_attempt@photo_class:utility]].

One utility poster-finding story says “Google Photos threw them up immediately,” implying no prolonged trying [[story|90c8b5f8d8913d764335d981d06c5dc02200c937:0]].

Interpretation: This uses a proxy (time spent trying) from public stories, not a user failure rate, and question 8.1 is sparsely coded — 30 coded, 85 not stated — so treat it cautiously [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]] [[analysis_coverage|8.1]].

*Want to see the same cut for other kinds?*

rows.question: What share of stories about photos kept for both sentimental and practical reasons fail at search?
rows.restated: What share of stories about photos kept for both sentimental and practical reasons first went wrong at search (stage 5)?
rows.gap: no core stories are about both photos, so nothing can be said about that group
rows.text:
We cannot answer for photos kept for both sentimental and practical reasons; there are no core stories in that group, so the share is unknown [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]].

Interpretation: As a proxy, here is where search first went wrong for each single-purpose group. For sentimental photos, fail at search is 27% (13 of 48; 17%–41%) · directional [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]]. For unclear, it is 33% (15 of 46; 21%–47%) · directional [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:unclear]]. For utility, it is 3 of 21 [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:utility]].

One person wrote, "I was able to go on my Google photos and went back to my first beatels photo" [[story|b2358d9efca162742579284a99c00a353586c178:0]].

These are shares of public stories, not user success rates [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]].

*Want to see adjacent stories included too?*

rows.question: How many core stories are there, and from how many different people?
rows.restated: How many CORE stories are in the corpus, and from how many distinct people were they posted?
rows.text:
There are 115 core stories from 109 different people. [[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]

The share is 115 of the stories corpus, posted by 109 authors. [[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]

One person put it simply: "i found my old baby photos in this app tysm". [[story|e7e4eb6a20b124405577ba1cd0fa0775014739c9:0]]

This count is below what the engine was designed for, so treat it as thin. [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]

*Want the adjacent count and authors too?*

rows.question: How many core stories first go wrong because search did not understand or match what was typed?
rows.restated: How many CORE stories first went wrong at the stage where search did not understand or match what was typed (stage 5)?
rows.text:
About a quarter of core stories first go wrong because search did not understand or match what was typed [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]].

27% (31 of 115) [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]].

One person wrote, "Google Photos: no result for vomit" while trying to find a specific memory [[story|88a83897e2c872e72ac85967d7fc5c158d43bbb0:0]].

This is a share of public stories, not a user success rate [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]].

*Want the split by sentimental vs utility?*

rows.question: And how does that split by kind of photo?
rows.restated: How does the stage where retrieval first goes wrong split by kind of photo (sentimental, utility, both, unclear)?
rows.text:
Search not understanding what they typed shows up across kinds of photos, with similar directional shares where we can compute them [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:unclear]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:utility]].
Among sentimental stories, 27% (13 of 48; 17%–41%) · directional first went wrong at Stage 5, while 35% (17 of 48; 23%–50%) · directional had nothing go wrong [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:sentimental]].
One person said, "I wanted to find some old fall photos and searched ‘forest’ in my gallery. this was the first result. 12/10 no notes." [[story|346adeec584d4ac2df9090145e995deb4acb616e:0]].
Utility stories are counts only: 3 of 21 at Stage 5, 8 of 21 at Stage 0, 6 of 21 at Stage 9 [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:utility]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:utility]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:utility]], and unclear shows 33% (15 of 46; 21%–47%) · directional at Stage 5 and 33% (15 of 46; 21%–47%) · directional with nothing wrong [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:unclear]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:unclear]].
This split is directional and based on public stories, not user rates [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]], [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]].

*Want to see the same split by failure owner?*

rows.question: Does that differ for utility photos?
rows.restated: Is what people typically type into search first different for utility photos compared with other photo types?
rows.gap: only 21 utility stories — under the 30 needed for a share, so only counts can be given
rows.text:
Interpretation: We can’t say utility differs; the utility subset is too small to generalize, but we can report its counts alongside directional shares for other kinds [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]].

Across core stories that state a first query, sentimental shows single-noun starts at 23% (11 of 48; 13%–37%) · directional, while utility has 3 of 21 single-noun starts and 2 of 21 several-keyword starts; unclear shows 11% (5 of 46; 5%–23%) · directional single-noun, 4% (2 of 46; 1%–15%) · directional several-keyword, and 2% (1 of 46; 0%–11%) · directional named-entity [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:sentimental]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=full_natural_description@photo_class:sentimental]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:unclear]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=several_keywords@photo_class:unclear]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=named_entity@photo_class:unclear]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:utility]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=several_keywords@photo_class:utility]].

One utility poster started with a noun-like token — “I put in "VIN" to search for my proof of insurance I KNOW I have multiple copies of.” [[story|33dd763b1d8fb1aac1afd0a4f6fcb1cec82b40ef:0]].

These are shares of coded public stories, not user or query shares [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]].

*Want the raw counts by each query shape?*

rows.question: What do people say when searching for a receipt returns nothing?
rows.restated: When searching for a receipt returns no results, what do people say (how do they describe/search/complain) in these public stories?
rows.text:
People say they typed a plain word like “receipt,” got nothing back, and then express annoyance or doubt about search itself [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.6=zero_results@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:6.5=nothing@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:9.4=aftermath:loss_or_annoyance@photo_class:_all]].

17% (19 of 115) opened with a single noun; zero-results appears in 2% (2 of 115); and 17% (19 of 115) said the results reminded them of nothing [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.6=zero_results@photo_class:_all]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:6.5=nothing@photo_class:_all]].

One person wrote, "I couldn't find the receipt for my laptop, 'receipt' returned nothing." [[story|probe-inj-04]]

Interpretation: Some utility searches also start with a short keyword or a couple words like “scrap receipt,” and people then vent that search “doesn’t show anything” or is “useless” [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=several_keywords@photo_class:utility]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.6=zero_results@photo_class:_all]] [[story|0ef3821f2d59998617a4b53f428fd49c9a22d2ff:0]] [[story|aec545954f160928ad65ebbf35950d747f907caf:0]]; this rests on a thin core [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]].

rows.text:
I could not write an answer to this that passed every check, so the draft is withheld and what follows is built from the evidence directly [[analysis_method_flags|no_gold_standard]].

The stories cannot support all of it: parts of this question reach past what the stories cover [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]].

The question takes as given something these stories do not show; the counts below are what they do show [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]].

- core stories where NOTHING went wrong (Stage 9: found, or found by accident) — 33% (38 of 115) [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]]
- core stories first going wrong at Stage 5 (Does search understand it?) — 27% (31 of 115) [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]]
- core stories first going wrong at Stage 0 (Is the photo there to find?) — 17% (20 of 115) [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:_all]]
- A story this rests on, to read in full [[story|probe-inj-06]]

Every share here is a share of coded public stories [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]].
